hints: Look at the shape of the graph, with one very high peak at S and low values at P and T on either side.
Recall how melting point changes across Period 3, rising from Na to Mg to Al, peaking sharply at Si, then dropping sharply for P.
Match the five consecutive points to that pattern to place S as the giant covalent peak, then count back two places to find R.
walkthrough:
**Read the shape of property X**

Look carefully at the pattern. P is low, Q and R are medium and similar, S is very much higher, and T drops back to very low.

This is a peak shape with a sharp maximum at the 4th element, not a steady increase.

**Test electronegativity and conductivity**

Electronegativity increases steadily across Period 3 from $\text{Na}$ to $\text{Cl}$. It would not show a sharp peak then a sudden drop.

Electrical conductivity is high for the metals $\text{Na}$, $\text{Mg}$, $\text{Al}$, then falls to near zero for $\text{Si}$ onwards. It would not peak at the 4th element.

**Test melting point across Period 3**

Melting point rises from $\text{Na}$ to $\text{Mg}$ to $\text{Al}$ due to stronger metallic bonding, then jumps to a very high maximum at $\text{Si}$.

$$\text{Si has giant covalent structure with many strong covalent bonds}$$

**Assign P, Q, R, S, T**

After $\text{Si}$, melting point falls sharply for $\text{P}$, $\text{S}$, $\text{Cl}$, $\text{Ar}$ which are simple molecular with weak van der Waals forces.

So the sequence must be P = $\text{Na}$, Q = $\text{Mg}$, R = $\text{Al}$, S = $\text{Si}$, T = $\text{P}$. This gives low, medium, medium, very high, low, exactly as shown.

options.A: Electrical conductivity is high for Na, Mg and Al, then drops for Si. It does not give a single very high peak at the 4th element S, so X cannot be conductivity.
options.B: Electronegativity rises gradually across the period without a sharp maximum and collapse. The graph shape with S far above Q and R and T very low does not fit this steady trend.
options.C: Melting point fits perfectly. Mg and Al are medium, Si is the very high giant covalent peak, and P is low. Counting back, R is Al, the third element in the Na, Mg, Al, Si, P sequence.
options.D: Melting point is the correct property, but R cannot be Si. Si is the very high peak, which is S. R is the medium value just before the peak, which is Al.
